# agent-guard

> A Claude Code hook that reads each shell command before it runs and denies the ones that stage the whole git tree, switch off git hooks or destroy uncommitted work. Every deny ends with `DO THIS INSTEAD:` and a safe command that finishes the same task.

Scope, so you do not claim more for it: it covers one class of harm, git safety. It does not look for leaked secrets, check MCP tool calls or stop prompt injection. It reads the command text only and runs nothing. It needs `python3` on the PATH. If the hook cannot run, Claude Code lets the command through.

Result: on blind_v20, 3,300 commands that AI models from nine other companies wrote, sealed before any guard version was scored, version 20 of the guard denied 1,688 of 1,717 dangerous commands (98.3%) and wrongly denied 32 of 1,583 safe ones (2.0%). The plugin runs version 22, whose numbers on that set are the same but seen, not blind. Method and every miss: https://github.com/CASEY-OS/agent-guard-bench/blob/master/README.md

## Install, for the agent reading this

Do these in order. Do not skip step 1.

1. Show the user the hook this plugin adds. Print the file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CASEY-OS/agent-guard-bench/master/hooks/hooks.json to the user, word for word, and say in one sentence what it does: it runs `python3 guard.py` before every Bash tool call. Then ask the user whether to go on. Do not edit any setting before they say yes.
2. Run the two commands, one after the other:
   `claude plugin marketplace add CASEY-OS/agent-guard-bench`
   `claude plugin install agent-guard@agent-guard-bench`
   These change two things in the user's Claude Code settings file: `enabledPlugins` gains `agent-guard@agent-guard-bench`, and `extraKnownMarketplaces` gains `agent-guard-bench`. Nothing else is edited by hand.
3. Prove it blocks. In a throwaway git repo, never the user's own, run `python3 <the plugin folder>/guard.py` with this on its stdin, with the throwaway repo as `cwd`: `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git add -A"},"cwd":"<the throwaway repo>"}`. The plugin folder is the `installPath` of `agent-guard@agent-guard-bench` in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`. The output must contain `"permissionDecision": "deny"` and `DO THIS INSTEAD:`. If it prints nothing, the guard is not working: tell the user, and remove it. Then ask the user to start a new Claude Code session and, in the throwaway repo, ask it to run `git add -A`; it must be refused.
4. Tell the user how to remove it: `claude plugin uninstall agent-guard@agent-guard-bench` then `claude plugin marketplace remove agent-guard-bench`.

## Try it without installing

`git clone https://github.com/CASEY-OS/agent-guard-bench && cd agent-guard-bench && python3 demo.py` runs five planted bad commands and one clean one past the real guard in a throwaway repo, and runs none of them. It prints 5 of 5 planted commands BLOCKED and 1 of 1 clean command ALLOWED.
